messages.body_plain:
I must confess I don't know where your error is at, but I commonly use
a strategy for getting these things right.

At the local R I do:
ifolder = "/airline/data"
idata = rhread(ifolder, type=type,max=max)   #fill in type and max
map.keys = lapply(idata,function(kv) k[[1]])
map.values = lapply(idata,function(kv) k[[2]])

And then test my manipulations.  From there I paste it all into the
appropriate pieces of the MapReduce expressions.

>

>
> map <- expression({

>    if(substr(r,1,4)!='Year') strsplit(r,",")[[1]]
>  }))
>  mu <- rep(1,nrow(y));yr <- y[,1]; mn=y[,2];dy=y[,3]

>  hr <- convertHHMM(y[,7])

>  d <- data.frame(depart= depart,sdepart = sdepart
>                ,arrive = arrive,sarrive =sarrive
>                ,carrier = y[,9],origin = y[,17]
>                ,dest=y[,18],dist = y[,19], year=yr, month-mn, day=dy
>                ,cancelled=y[,22], stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
>  d <- d[order(d$sdepart),]
>  rhcollect(d[c(1,nrow(d)),"sdepart"],d)})
>
> reduce <- expression(
>    reduce = {
>      lapply(reduce.values,function(i)
>             rhcollect(reduce.key,i))}
>    )
> mapred <- list(rhipe_map_buff_size=5000)
> z <- rhmr(map=map,reduce=reduce,setup=setup,inout=c("text","sequence")
>          ,ifolder="/airline/data/",ofolder="/airline/
> blocks",mapred=mapred,orderby="numeric")
> rhex(z)
>
> I made the following mods to three lines of that MapReduce job based
> on my research for ordering by the distance traveled ("dist" field):
>
>  d <- d[order(d$dist),]
>
>  rhcollect(d[c(1,nrow(d)),"dist"],d)
>
>  z <-
> rhmr(map=map,reduce=reduce,setup=setup,inout=c("text","sequence")
>          ,ifolder="/airline/data/",ofolder="/airline/
> blocks",mapred=mapred,orderby="integer")

> However, this doesn't work.  The dataset I get back isn't ordered by

> greatly appreciate any help.
>
> Thanks in advance,
> Jeremy

messages.subject: Shuffle Problem
messages.body_plain:
Hello All,

I've got a problem I've been struggling with for days.  Here's the
deal.

I've got some bug report data:
identifier	name	ver	class	wmc	dit	noc	cbo	rfc	lcom
1	ant	1.7	org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.rmic.RmicAdapterFactory	3	1	0
10	18	3
2	ant	1.7
org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.optional.perforce.FStatP4OutputHandler	5
2	0
3	ant	1.7
org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.optional.junit.OutErrSummaryJUnitResultFormatter
1
4	ant	1.7
org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.optional.perforce.P4HandlerAdapter	8	1	9
13	20

I truncated it so it would fit in this window.  Essentially, it's 5
merged datasets from the PROMISE software engineering repository (Ant,
Lucene, Camel, etc).  I want to calculate the total number of bugs for
the Ant classes, lucene classes, camel classes, etc.  I iterate this
with the Map Reduce below.  I'm expecting Hadoop/Rhipe to 'shuffle/
merge' the keys, but it's not doing it.

library(Rhipe)
rhinit(TRUE,TRUE,buglevel=2000)

map.test <- expression({
  y <- do.call("rbind",map.values)

  if(nrow(y) > 0)
  {
     for( i in 1:nrow(y))
     {
          x<-y[i, ]
          key<-x[2] #codebase
         value<-as.numeric(x[25]) #bugs
         rhcollect(key,value)
      }
  }

})

reduce <- expression(
    post={
      rhcollect(reduce.key, reduce.values)
   }
)

mapred <-
list(rhipe_map_buff_size=20,mapred.task.timeout=0,mapred.reduce.tasks=1)
z <-
rhmr(map=map.test,reduce=reduce,inout=c("sequence","sequence"),ifolder="/
apacheOut/blocks_01/p*"
          ,ofolder="/apacheOut/blocks_04",mapred=mapred,
combiner=FALSE)
rhex(z)

The Map function kicks out 3113 records, as I would expect, each with
the name of the software and the number of bugs like this:
(lucene, [0,1,4,0,0...])

However, when I look at the results from the debugging reduce I'm
using, it's the same list that comes out of the Map ... all 3113
records, without them being shuffle/merged.  Tried dozens of things...
nothing seems to matter.  Not sure if it makes a difference, but I'm
using Cloudera's CDH 3.5 running in Pseudo Distributed mode in a
single VM.

Would appreciate any ideas as to why the shuffle/merge isn't occuring.

Thanks,
Jeremy

messages.body_plain:
Hello,
1) What is an element of map.values? A line look likes

1       ant     1.7
org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.rmic.RmicAdapterFactory  3       1
010      18      3

?
I shall assume that y is a matrix of fields corresponding to the
example you gave.
2nd field is codebase, 25th field is the number of bugs.
I guess you want total number of bugs by codebase?
Better map:
map.test <- expression({  y <- do.call('rbind',map.values)  ## how can
nrow(y) == 0???  if(nrow(y)>0){    apply(y[,c(2,25)],1,function(r){
  rhcollect( r[1], as.numeric(r[2]))    })  }})
So you want to aggregate your values e.g.

 (lucene, [0,1,4,0,0...])
(I thought sum?)
1) If you wanted an aggregate
reduce <- expression(  pre={ y <-  c() }  ,reduce = { y <- c(y,
unlist(reduce.values)) }  ,post = { rhcollect(reduce.key, y ) })
mapred <- list(rhipe_map_buff_size=20,mapred.task.timeout=0)z <-
rhmr(map=map.test          ,reduce=reduce
,inout=c("seq","seq"),ifolder="/apacheOut/blocks_01/p*"
,ofolder="/apacheOut/blocks_04"          ,mapred=mapred,
,combiner=TRUE)rhex(z)

2) You want a sum?reduce <- expression(  pre={ y <-  0 }  ,reduce = {
y <-  y+ sum( unlist(reduce.values),na.rm=TRUE) }  ,post = {
rhcollect(reduce.key, y ) })
The other code is the same.
Hope this helpsSaptarshi

Thanks Saptarshi!  I learn by example, so it definitely helps. And, I

However, when I run my output through the reducer example you
provided, it still comes out as a list of 3113 records.  So the
"special sauce" is in the Mapper, or so it would seem. Is there some
added dimensionality to the data that prevents this from being

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] rhwrite
messages.body_plain:
rhwrite only writes as SequencFiles. Also, rhwrite really ruins your
data frame - each column is written as a value.
Not what you'd expect ...

if you want data, write to local text file and then do rhput.

And if you want data frames (say M x N rows)  to be written in chunks,
create a list with each entry a  M_i X N rows where Sum(M_i,i=1,...)
== M

HTH
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: Hadoop version 20.203
messages.body_plain:
I think that previous response was to one of my groups emails about
troubleshooting an R 2.14 issue.  That issue a whole different thing.
This is a complete brand new cluster.  Not the rossmann RCAC hadoop
cluster and not Dr. Cleveland's private cluster.   It is new one
administered by RCAC that has never had a working Rhipe on it.  This
cluster uses R 2.11.

Regarding the cluster I am asking about the only information I have to
provide really is the output from this simple MapReduce job.  I find
the access permission security error interesting.  In asking this
question I was trying to figure out if 20.203 was known to be good
with Rhipe, so I could rule out the particular hadoop being used and
move on to system configuration issues.

library(Rhipe)
rhinit()
#rhoptions(runner=sprintf("%s/rhipe.runner.sh <http://rhipe.runner.sh>",Sys.getenv("HOME")))
rhoptions(runner=sprintf("%s/mapreduce.runner.sh <http://mapreduce.runner.sh>",Sys.getenv("HOME")))

ofolder = "/wsc/jrounds/garbage/garbage1"
inout = c("lapply", "sequence")
N = 2
jobname = ofolder
map = expression({
    for(i in seq_along(map.values)){
        rhcollect(1,i)
    }
})
mr = rhmr(map = map, inout=inout,ofolder=ofolder, N=N, jobname =
jobname	, mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks=2))
ex = rhex(mr)

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Hadoop version 20.203
messages.body_plain:
We ran into a similar issue (code:127) in our cluster.

After debugging the issue, it was related to missing libR.so in LD_LIBRARY_PATH and the forked task jvms
(which need -Djava.library.path=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib to be passed)

This was fixed like so:

1) Add
  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
 a) to hadoop user's shell env.
 b) to $HADOOP_HOME/conf/hadoop-env.sh
 export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

2) Add to $HADOOP_HOME/conf/mapred-site.xml

<property>
 <name>mapred.child.jvm.opts</name>
 <value>-Xmx1g -Xms1g  -Djava.library.path=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib </value>
</property>

Let me know if this works in your environment,
thanks,
Sri

messages.body_plain:
Interesting. Any insight why some clusters would need a special entry
for mapred.child.jvm.opts while others wouldn't?

On Dec 15, 3:07 pm, SriSatish Ambati <srisatish.amb...@gmail.com>
wrote:

> We ran into a similar issue (code:127) in our cluster.
>
> After debugging the issue, it was related to missing libR.so in
> LD_LIBRARY_PATH and the forked task jvms
> (which need -Djava.library.path=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib to be passed)
>
> This was fixed like so:
>
> 1) Add
>   export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
>  a) to hadoop user's shell env.
>  b) to $HADOOP_HOME/conf/hadoop-env.sh
>  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
>
> 2) Add to $HADOOP_HOME/conf/mapred-site.xml
>
> <property>
>  <name>mapred.child.jvm.opts</name>

>  <value>-Xmx1g -Xms1g  *-Djava.library.path=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib* </value>

> </property>
>
> Let me know if this works in your environment,
> thanks,
> Sri

messages.body_plain:
For what it's worth, I've been running on 0.2.203.  On a small cluster
where I installed and configured everything myself, I could only make
it work if I was logged in as the hadoop user.  On our institutional
cluster, however, I've been running it with no problems.  (As an
aside, I'm really curious about how it will work on the nextgen
mapreduce 0.23 stuff from HortonWorks - have you played with this,
Saptarshi?)

The error code 127 has been a linking issue for me, as Sri mentioned.
You may be aware of this trick, but what has helped me figure these
out is the following:

Make a shell script that is executed by the the runner set in
rhoptions to help you diagnose the problem, called, for example
Rsetup.sh:

#!/bin/bash
ldd _path_to_imperious.so_ > ~/lddoutput
exec R CMD _path_to_imperious.so_ --slave --silent --vanilla --max-
ppsize=100000 --max-nsize=1G

Then set it in R before running your Rhipe job with:

rhoptions(runner="_path_to_Rsetup.sh_")

Now when you run a simple job, it will output the ldd output to the
file ~/lddoutput, which you can then inspect to see if there failures
to link.  If you are paranoid about environment variables being set
correctly on each node, you can also add those in to the Rsetup.sh
script as well, which might be overkill, before the final exec line
such as:

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=(path to Rlib.so should be part of this)
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=...
...

I like Saptarshi's suggestion of moving R to the nodes for every job.
We have this setup by default on our institutional cluster since all
nodes can see my home directory, and it makes things really nice.

messages.subject: Linking problems with RHIPE
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Xavier had some build and linking issues.

Xavier and others: Sorry you had to go through this mess. I;m happy you manages to fix this, i'll push a change.
Thank you for your efforts.

Forwarded message:

Hello Saptarshi,

After a week of nightmare, I finally found the problem. It was
actually in Makevars.in. I had a friend explaining me what's wrong,
and actually most compilers are friendly enough to let it go.

The issue is that ${PKG_LIBS} and ${RLIB} should actually be at the
end of line54. It seems that during link edition, the norm (posix? not
sure...) would require to put dependencies in order: if liba.so links
to libb.so, then you shall not write -lb -la. If they link to each
other, -lb -la -lb should be ok (but I couldn't test, I just repeat
what I heard on the phone).

So in our case, putting the -lR and -lprotobuf after the list of
compiled objects is enough to solve the problem. I sent a private
email (I didn't find how to reply on the group) to the guy there:
https://groups.google.com/group/rhipe/browse_thread/thread/a3b5b778be444c9f/acabdb406aa52117
but couldn't find how to make the comment public. I am pretty sure
this would solve his problem as well.

Oh because, yes, now I can compile imperious.so, thus Rhipe :) I'll
try tomorrow to see if other problems are solved with this tweek.

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Hadoop version 20.203
messages.body_plain:
HBase is there. But in order to use HBase as inputformat, it is best to write ones own HBaseInputFormat
and it include the JAR file using rhmr(,...jar=)

the tricky thing is hbase keys and values are raw bytes. So it can be passed over to RHIPE but how does

on intelligently specify the rowkeys (as raw bytes in RHIPE)?.
A default of text keys and raw bytes for values is very doable.

messages.subject: Re: RHive (integrating R and Hive) connection issues
messages.subject_clean: RHive (integrating R and Hive) connection issues
messages.body_plain:
Hi Som,

I think I had a similar problem to you and just found a solution. All
I had to do was to run a hiveserver service on the head-node. More
specifically, I just started 'hive --service hiveserver 2> /tmp/
hiveserver.log &' on my development server. Now, if I run
'rhive.connect()' in R, all works great and as expected! I should say
that I am using RStudio Server on the same server which runs the
Hiveserver. This works excellent!

Enjoy,

Ralf Herbrich

On Dec 4, 10:43 am, Shekhar <shekhar2...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,

> jobtracker.thrift.address?
